skill.name: api-testing-observability-api-mock
skill.description: Design realistic API mock services for development, integration testing, demos, and contract validation.
skill.summary: Create stateful API mocks with scenarios, fixtures, testing integrations, deployment guidance, and documentation.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives in examples or Markdown paths, including local mock URLs, config dictionary lookups, and backticked resource names. Two external Swagger UI CDN references are confirmed as low risk because generated documentation would load third-party assets. I also found a low data-handling concern where mock request tracking stores full headers and request bodies.

remediation.issue: Generated documentation loads Swagger UI assets from unpkg.com.
remediation.suggestion: Pin exact versions and integrity hashes, or self-host the Swagger UI JavaScript and CSS assets.

remediation.issue: Mock request tracking can store full headers and request bodies.
remediation.suggestion: Redact Authorization, Cookie, Set-Cookie, and sensitive body fields before storing request history.

content.value_statement: Mock APIs are hard to keep realistic, aligned with contracts, and useful for tests. This skill helps design stateful mocks, scenarios, fixtures, deployment steps, and documentation.
actual_capabilities: Define mock server routes, middleware, and request matching behavior.
Create stateful stubs with scenarios, sequences, delays, and error responses.
Generate realistic mock data from schemas and reusable fixtures.
Validate mock behavior against API contracts such as OpenAPI.
Plan testing integrations for Jest, pytest, and request verification.
Draft deployment and documentation patterns for mock services.
limitations: It does not test production systems or live partner integrations.
It needs an API contract or clear expected behavior to produce useful mocks.
Generated examples still need environment-specific review before deployment.
It should not use real customer data or production secrets in fixtures.

use_cases.title: Frontend Development Before Backend Readiness
use_cases.description: Create realistic endpoints so frontend teams can build and test without waiting for backend completion.

use_cases.title: Contract-Based Integration Testing
use_cases.description: Generate mock responses from API contracts and validate expected status codes, schemas, and error shapes.

use_cases.title: Reliable Demo Environments
use_cases.description: Build scenario-driven mocks that show happy paths, failures, latency, and degraded service behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Mock API
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a mock API plan for this frontend feature. Ask for missing endpoints, response shapes, auth behavior, errors, and latency.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Mock Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate a FastAPI mock service from this API contract. Include routes, sample fixtures, error scenarios, and run instructions.

prompt_templates.title: Design Test Scenarios
prompt_templates.prompt: Design scenario-based mocks for happy path, rate limits, expired sessions, and degraded performance. Include reset behavior and request verification.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Mocking Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a full API mock strategy for this service migration. Cover contract validation, stateful data, test integration, deployment, and documentation.

output_examples.input: Create mocks for a user profile API.
output: A route plan for profile retrieval, updates, validation errors, and not-found cases.
Fixture guidance for realistic users, addresses, preferences, and account states.
Test scenario notes for success, expired sessions, and slow responses.

output_examples.input: Mock a payment provider for local testing.
output: Scenario definitions for approved, declined, pending, refunded, and webhook delivery states.
Request verification guidance for idempotency keys, headers, and retry behavior.
Safety notes to avoid real cards, production credentials, and customer records.

output_examples.input: Turn an OpenAPI contract into test mocks.
output: A contract-driven mock plan with endpoints, response variants, and schema checks.
A validation checklist for status codes, required fields, and documented error responses.

best_practices: Start from a current API contract before adding custom behavior.
Use deterministic fixtures by default, then add controlled randomness when needed.
Clearly label mock endpoints and keep them separate from production services.
anti_patterns: Do not point live production traffic at a mock service.
Do not store real secrets, tokens, payment data, or customer records in fixtures.
Do not create mocks that hide contract drift or missing backend behavior.

faq.question: What kind of API work is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for designing mock APIs used in development, testing, demonstrations, and contract validation.

faq.question: Can it generate a complete mock server plan?
faq.answer: Yes. It can outline routes, state handling, fixtures, scenarios, test hooks, deployment, and documentation.

faq.question: Does it replace integration testing against real services?
faq.answer: No. It supports earlier testing, but real service validation is still required before release.

faq.question: Can it work from an OpenAPI contract?
faq.answer: Yes. The playbook includes contract loading, mock generation, and response validation patterns.

faq.question: How should sensitive data be handled?
faq.answer: Use synthetic fixtures only. Redact tokens, cookies, and personal data from request history and logs.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
